title: 1 Samuel Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 19.

questions.question: Who did Saul command to kill David?
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan and all his servants
questions.explanation: Saul spoke to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David, as stated in 1 Samuel 19:1.

questions.question: What did Jonathan do after hearing that Saul wanted to kill David?
options: He told David and advised him to hide
He told Saul to kill David immediately
He joined Saul in trying to kill David
questions.correctAnswer: He told David and advised him to hide
questions.explanation: Jonathan told David about Saul's plan and advised him to take heed and hide himself in a secret place, as recorded in 1 Samuel 19:2.

questions.question: Where did Jonathan say he would stand to speak with his father about David?
options: In the field where David was
questions.correctAnswer: In the field where David was
questions.explanation: Jonathan said he would stand beside his father in the field where David was and commune with him about David, as found in 1 Samuel 19:3.

questions.question: What reasoning did Jonathan give Saul to convince him not to harm David?
options: David has done no wrong and saved Israel by killing the Philistine
David is a relative of Saul
David had paid Saul a large sum of money
David promised to serve Saul forever
questions.correctAnswer: David has done no wrong and saved Israel by killing the Philistine
questions.explanation: Jonathan reminded Saul that David had not sinned against him and that he had saved Israel by killing the Philistine, as stated in 1 Samuel 19:4-5.

questions.question: How did Saul respond to Jonathan's appeal regarding David?
options: He swore David would not be slain
questions.correctAnswer: He swore David would not be slain
questions.explanation: Saul hearkened to Jonathan's voice and swore that David should not be slain, as found in 1 Samuel 19:6.

questions.question: What did Jonathan do after Saul's oath concerning David?
options: Called David, told him all, and brought him to Saul
Warned Saul to kill David at once
questions.correctAnswer: Called David, told him all, and brought him to Saul
questions.explanation: Jonathan called David, showed him all that Saul had said, and brought him to Saul where David was in his presence as before, according to 1 Samuel 19:7.

questions.question: What happened during the next war mentioned in the chapter?
options: David fought the Philistines and slew many
David was captured by the Philistines
Jonathan led the army to defeat
Saul made peace with the Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: David fought the Philistines and slew many
questions.explanation: During the war, David went out and fought with the Philistines, killing them with great slaughter, as stated in 1 Samuel 19:8.

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan was pleased with David and protected him from Saul's wrath.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan delighted much in David and warned him of Saul's intent to kill him, as per 1 Samuel 19:2.

questions.question: True or False: Saul immediately killed David after Jonathan spoke to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Saul hearkened to Jonathan and swore that David should not be slain, so he did not kill him immediately, as shown in 1 Samuel 19:6.

questions.question: True or False: David was brought before Saul and was in his presence as before after Jonathan's intervention.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past, according to 1 Samuel 19:7.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter states that David fled immediately after Jonathan warned him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonathan told David to hide until morning; David did not flee immediately after the warning, as per 1 Samuel 19:2.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 19, which event comes first?
options: Saul sending messengers to kill David
Saul being filled with an evil spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan warning David to hide
questions.explanation: Jonathan's warning to David to hide occurs first in the chapter, specifically in 1 Samuel 19:2, before other events like Saul sending messengers or David fighting the Philistines.

questions.question: What did Jonathan say about David's works toward Saul?
questions.correctAnswer: They have been very good
questions.explanation: Jonathan spoke good of David to Saul, saying his works have been very good toward Saul, as recorded in 1 Samuel 19:4.

questions.question: Who did Jonathan say had wrought a great salvation for all Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Jonathan said that the LORD wrought a great salvation for all Israel when David slew the Philistine, as found in 1 Samuel 19:5.

questions.question: What was Saul doing when the evil spirit from the LORD came upon him according to this chapter?
options: Sitting in his house with his javelin in his hand
questions.correctAnswer: Sitting in his house with his javelin in his hand
questions.explanation: The evil spirit from the LORD came upon Saul as he sat in his house with his javelin in his hand, as described in 1 Samuel 19:9.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Saul doing when the evil spirit from the LORD came upon him, according to 1 Samuel 19?
options: Sitting in his house with his javelin in his hand
questions.correctAnswer: Sitting in his house with his javelin in his hand
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:9 states that the evil spirit from the LORD was upon Saul as he sat in his house with his javelin in his hand, and David was playing with his hand.

questions.question: How did David escape when Saul tried to kill him with a javelin?
options: He slipped away out of Saul's presence
He fought Saul and disarmed him
He prayed for protection and Saul relented
questions.correctAnswer: He slipped away out of Saul's presence
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 19:10, Saul sought to smite David, but David slipped away out of Saul's presence, and Saul's javelin struck the wall instead.

questions.question: What warning did Michal give David about Saul's plans?
options: If you save not your life this night, tomorrow you shall be slain
Saul has forgiven you and wants peace
You must flee to the Philistines immediately
questions.correctAnswer: If you save not your life this night, tomorrow you shall be slain
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:11 records that Michal warned David, telling him that if he did not save his life that night, he would be killed the next day.

questions.question: How did Michal help David escape from Saul’s messengers?
options: She let him down through a window
She hid him in the attic
She told Saul he was at a friend's house
She disguised him as a servant
questions.correctAnswer: She let him down through a window
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:12 states that Michal let David down through a window so he could flee and escape Saul's messengers.

questions.question: What did Michal place in David’s bed to deceive Saul’s messengers?
options: An image covered with a cloth and a pillow of goats' hair
questions.correctAnswer: An image covered with a cloth and a pillow of goats' hair
questions.explanation: Michal took an image (a household idol or figure), laid it in David’s bed with a pillow of goats' hair for a bolster, and covered it with a cloth to make it appear David was in bed (1 Samuel 19:13).

questions.question: When Saul’s messengers arrived to take David, what reason did Michal give for David’s absence?
options: He has fled to the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: He is sick
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 19:14, Michal told Saul’s messengers that David was sick, thus preventing them from discovering his escape.

questions.question: What did Saul command his messengers to do when they returned to get David from bed?
options: Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him
Take him quietly to the palace
Warn him to flee the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:15 records Saul’s command to his messengers to bring David to him in the bed so he could kill him.

questions.question: What did Saul’s messengers find when they came to get David from the bed the second time?
options: An image in the bed with a pillow of goats' hair
questions.correctAnswer: An image in the bed with a pillow of goats' hair
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 19:16, the messengers found the image with a goats' hair pillow in the bed, deceiving them into thinking David was lying there.

questions.question: Why did Michal say she deceived Saul and sent David away?
options: David told me to let him go; why should I kill thee?
I wanted to protect the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: David told me to let him go; why should I kill thee?
questions.explanation: Michal responded to Saul by saying David told her to let him go and questioned why she should kill Saul (1 Samuel 19:17).

questions.question: Where did David flee after escaping Saul’s attempts on his life?
questions.correctAnswer: To Samuel at Ramah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:18 shows David fled to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done, after which they dwelt in Naioth.

questions.question: What happened to Saul’s messengers when they came to take David at Naioth in Ramah?
options: The Spirit of God came upon them and they prophesied
They captured David and returned him to Saul
They were chased away by Samuel
They hid and waited for David to come out
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God came upon them and they prophesied
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 20 state that when Saul’s messengers saw the company of prophets prophesying and Samuel standing over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers and they also prophesied.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 19:14 promise will happen if Michal deceives Saul’s messengers as instructed in 1 Samuel 19:13?
options: The messengers will think David is sick and not find him
David will be captured and imprisoned
Michal will be punished by Saul
questions.correctAnswer: The messengers will think David is sick and not find him
questions.explanation: Michal’s deception with the image in the bed (verse 13) leads to her telling the messengers that David is sick (verse 14), preventing them from discovering his escape.

questions.question: What lesson about faith and obedience can be learned from David’s escape aided by Michal in 1 Samuel 19?
options: Trusting God and obeying those who help us can lead to deliverance
One must always fight physically to overcome enemies
Deception is the only way to survive trials
Avoid all relationships to prevent danger
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God and obeying those who help us can lead to deliverance
questions.explanation: David’s trust in God’s protection and obedience to Michal’s help (verses 11-12) show that faith combined with wise assistance leads to deliverance from danger.

questions.question: True or False: Saul’s messengers prophesied three separate times after encountering the Spirit of God at Naioth.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:21 states that Saul sent messengers multiple times, and each time they prophesied under the Spirit of God’s influence.

questions.question: True or False: Saul personally went to Naioth and prophesied there after the Spirit of God came upon him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 19:23-24 describe how Saul went to Naioth, the Spirit of God came upon him also, and he prophesied, stripping off his clothes and lying down naked all day and night.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 19.

questions.question: Why did Saul question Michal about deceiving him and sending away his enemy?
options: Because David had escaped from his house
Because Michal had hidden David in the city
Because Michal had told David to fight Saul
Because Saul wanted to bless David
questions.correctAnswer: Because David had escaped from his house
questions.explanation: Saul asked Michal why she deceived him and sent away his enemy, referring to David's escape (1 Samuel 19:17).

questions.question: Where did David flee after escaping from Saul, according to 1 Samuel 19?
questions.correctAnswer: Naioth in Ramah
questions.explanation: David fled to Samuel at Ramah and they dwelt in Naioth (1 Samuel 19:18).

questions.question: What happened to Saul’s messengers when they came to Naioth to capture David?
questions.correctAnswer: They began to prophesy
questions.explanation: Saul's messengers saw the company of prophets and the Spirit of God came upon them so that they prophesied (1 Samuel 19:20).

questions.question: How many times did Saul send messengers who ended up prophesying instead of capturing David?
questions.correctAnswer: Three times
questions.explanation: Saul sent messengers three times, and each time they prophesied (1 Samuel 19:21).

questions.question: What was Saul’s reaction when he went to Ramah and also began to prophesy?
options: He stripped off his clothes and lay naked all day and night
He prayed to God for guidance
questions.correctAnswer: He stripped off his clothes and lay naked all day and night
questions.explanation: Saul stripped off his clothes and prophesied before Samuel, lying naked all that day and night (1 Samuel 19:24).

questions.question: What is the significance of the Spirit of God coming upon Saul and his messengers causing them to prophesy?
options: It shows God’s power to override human intent
It was a sign of Saul’s blessing
It was a punishment for David
It was an illusion created by Samuel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s power to override human intent
questions.explanation: The Spirit of God coming upon Saul and his messengers to prophesy demonstrates divine intervention preventing Saul’s plans (1 Samuel 19:20-23).

questions.question: What did Michal place in David’s bed to deceive Saul’s messengers?
options: An image with a pillow of goats' hair
questions.correctAnswer: An image with a pillow of goats' hair
questions.explanation: Michal took an image and laid it in the bed with a pillow of goats' hair to mimic David (1 Samuel 19:13).

questions.question: True or False: Michal warned David that if he did not save his life that night, he would be slain the next day.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Michal informed David that Saul planned to kill him the next day if he did not escape that night (1 Samuel 19:11).

questions.question: What was Saul’s original intent toward David as indicated at the beginning of the chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: To kill David
questions.explanation: Saul commanded Jonathan and his servants to kill David (1 Samuel 19:1).

questions.question: How did Jonathan demonstrate his loyalty to David despite Saul’s intentions?
options: He protected David and informed him of Saul’s plans
He joined Saul in trying to kill David
He ignored both Saul and David
questions.correctAnswer: He protected David and informed him of Saul’s plans
questions.explanation: Jonathan warned David about Saul’s attempt to kill him and promised to communicate with Saul on David’s behalf (1 Samuel 19:2-3).

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by Saul prophesying and lying naked all day and night, causing people to say 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'
questions.correctAnswer: Irony
questions.explanation: The unexpected behavior of Saul, who sought to kill David but ends up prophesying and lying naked, creates situational irony (1 Samuel 19:24).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s Spirit coming upon a person causing unexpected prophetic behavior, similar to 1 Samuel 19?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 11:25
questions.explanation: Numbers 11:25 describes the Spirit of God coming upon the elders causing them to prophesy, paralleling the Spirit coming upon Saul and his messengers (1 Samuel 19:20-23).

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'Naioth' as used in the chapter where David and Samuel dwelt?
questions.correctAnswer: Habitations or dwellings
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Naioth' means 'habitations' or 'dwellings,' referring to the place where Samuel and David stayed (1 Samuel 19:18).

questions.question: True or False: Saul’s repeated sending of messengers who prophesied instead of capturing David demonstrates the failure of Saul’s plans.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text shows Saul’s failure as his messengers prophesied rather than capturing David, thwarting his plans (1 Samuel 19:20-21).

questions.question: Which New Testament event can be seen as a fulfillment of the theme of God’s Spirit causing unexpected prophetic action, similar to the Spirit coming upon Saul and his messengers?
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 2:1-4 (Pentecost)
questions.explanation: At Pentecost, the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples causing them to speak in tongues and prophesy, paralleling the Spirit’s effect on Saul and his messengers (1 Samuel 19:20-23).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is demonstrated by Jonathan's intervention to protect David from Saul's intent to kill him?
options: The doctrine of sanctification through human loyalty and intercession
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sanctification through human loyalty and intercession
questions.explanation: Jonathan's actions show how human loyalty and intercession can serve as instruments of God's protective sanctification, as seen in 1 Samuel 19:2-6 where Jonathan warns David and pleads with Saul.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is reflected by the 'evil spirit from the LORD' upon Saul in this chapter?
options: God's sovereignty over evil spirits to accomplish His purposes
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereignty over evil spirits to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: The evil spirit sent from the LORD upon Saul (1 Samuel 19:9) shows God's sovereign control over spiritual forces, using even an evil spirit to fulfill His divine plan, as also reflected in Job 1:12.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Michal deceiving Saul with an image illustrate a theological theme in this chapter?
options: The theme of human wisdom and protection in God's providence
questions.correctAnswer: The theme of human wisdom and protection in God's providence
questions.explanation: Michal's deception (1 Samuel 19:13-16) highlights human agency and wisdom operating within God's providential protection of David, showing how God uses human means to preserve His chosen servant.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is drawn from Saul's multiple attempts to kill David (verses 1 and 11) and David fleeing to Samuel at Naioth (verse 18)?
options: God's eternal decree of salvation and judgment
The doctrine of the church as a refuge and sanctuary for the persecuted
The doctrine of predestination and election
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the church as a refuge and sanctuary for the persecuted
questions.explanation: Saul's pursuit of David (1 Samuel 19:1,11) contrasted with David's refuge with Samuel at Naioth (19:18) illustrates how God provides spiritual sanctuary through His servants, foreshadowing the church as refuge for God's people, as in Psalm 46:1.

questions.question: What does the prophesying of Saul's messengers (verses 20-21) reveal about the nature of the Spirit of God in this chapter?
options: The Spirit of God is selective and can influence multiple people simultaneously
The Spirit of God only empowers kings
The Spirit of God is limited to one individual at a time
The Spirit of God is absent in times of conflict
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God is selective and can influence multiple people simultaneously
questions.explanation: The fact that Saul's messengers also prophesied upon encountering the Spirit (19:20-21) shows God's Spirit can empower multiple individuals simultaneously for His purposes, demonstrating divine sovereignty over spiritual gifts.

questions.question: From a Christological perspective, how does David's role as God's anointed persecuted by Saul foreshadow Jesus Christ?
options: David's kingship directly fulfills the Messiah's reign
David's persecution and escape prefigure Christ's suffering and ultimate vindication
questions.correctAnswer: David's persecution and escape prefigure Christ's suffering and ultimate vindication
questions.explanation: David's experience of being pursued by Saul yet preserved by God (1 Samuel 19) foreshadows Christ's suffering under hostile rulers and divine vindication, aligning with typology seen in Acts 2:30-31.

questions.question: What theological teaching about God's justice and human sinfulness is illustrated in Saul's attempt to kill David 'without a cause' as rebuked by Jonathan?
options: That God's justice always punishes innocent blood
That sin against innocent blood is a grievous offense before God
questions.correctAnswer: That sin against innocent blood is a grievous offense before God
questions.explanation: Jonathan's rebuke to Saul (19:4-5) emphasizes the severity of shedding innocent blood, revealing God's high regard for justice and highlighting human sinfulness when acting unjustly, consistent with Proverbs 6:16-17.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Saul stripping off his clothes and prophesying (verse 24) contribute to the chapter's theological message?
options: It shows Saul's final madness and loss of divine favor
It indicates Saul's repentance and restoration
It reveals the powerlessness of prophecy
It demonstrates Saul's humility before Samuel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Saul's final madness and loss of divine favor
questions.explanation: Saul stripping off his clothes and prophesying naked (19:24) symbolizes his spiritual and political humiliation, indicating his loss of divine favor and foreshadowing his downfall, reinforcing the consequences of rejecting God's anointed.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do verses 9 and 10 teach about the conflict between divine providence and human evil intentions?
options: Human plans always triumph over God's will
God's providence allows evil but ultimately protects His chosen
Evil spirits act independently of God
Divine providence is passive in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence allows evil but ultimately protects His chosen
questions.explanation: The evil spirit tormenting Saul (19:9) and Saul's failed attempt to kill David (19:10) illustrate that while God permits evil intentions, His providence ensures the protection and preservation of His chosen servant, as also seen in Romans 8:28.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by Samuel and the prophets dwelling together at Naioth, providing a spiritual refuge for David?
options: God's providential care and faithfulness to His servants
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential care and faithfulness to His servants
questions.explanation: The community at Naioth where David finds refuge (19:18-19) reveals God's providential care and faithfulness in protecting His servants through spiritual fellowship and prophetic ministry.

questions.question: How does Jonathan's promise to inform David of his father's intentions (verse 3) reflect theological truths about human agency and divine foreknowledge?
options: It shows that human agency is irrelevant when God knows all
It reveals that human agency operates within divine foreknowledge for God's purposes
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals that human agency operates within divine foreknowledge for God's purposes
questions.explanation: Jonathan's commitment to inform David (19:3) exemplifies how human choices and actions function under God's sovereign foreknowledge to accomplish divine plans, harmonizing divine sovereignty with human responsibility.

questions.question: What does the repeated sending of Saul's messengers who end up prophesying (verses 20-23) teach about the power of God's Spirit over human opposition?
options: God's Spirit can overpower and transform even those sent to oppose His will
God's Spirit is limited to spiritual leaders
Human opposition always frustrates God's Spirit
Prophecy is unrelated to God's Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: God's Spirit can overpower and transform even those sent to oppose His will
questions.explanation: The messengers sent by Saul who prophesy instead (19:20-23) demonstrate that God's Spirit has the power to overcome human opposition and redirect even enemies to serve His purposes, affirming divine sovereignty.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine inspiration of prophecy in 1 Samuel 19 is inconsistent because Saul's messengers prophesied unexpectedly. What does 1 Samuel 19:20-21 teach about the nature of God's Spirit in this context?
options: That the Spirit of God can sovereignly empower individuals regardless of initial intent to fulfill divine purposes
That prophecy is purely human invention
That God's Spirit is limited to the prophet Samuel
That the messengers were pretending to prophesy
questions.correctAnswer: That the Spirit of God can sovereignly empower individuals regardless of initial intent to fulfill divine purposes
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 show that although Saul sent messengers to capture David, God's Spirit came upon them and they prophesied instead, illustrating God's sovereign ability to use any person to accomplish His will, consistent with 2 Kings 3:15.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does David's military victory over the Philistines in verse 8 have to the broader biblical story of God's salvation history?
options: It foreshadows the ultimate victory of God's Anointed over evil
It depicts Israel's failure in war
It contradicts the theme of God's protection
It shows David as a political usurper
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the ultimate victory of God's Anointed over evil
questions.explanation: David's defeat of the Philistines (19:8) anticipates the Messiah's triumph over evil powers, linking to the broader salvation narrative where God's Anointed conquers spiritual enemies, as portrayed in Revelation 19:11-16.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from Jonathan's defense of David (verses 4-6) and Saul's oath not to kill David (verse 6)?
options: The doctrine of covenant loyalty and God's faithfulness to His promises
The doctrine of predestination without human responsibility
The doctrine of divine wrath without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenant loyalty and God's faithfulness to His promises
questions.explanation: Jonathan's plea (19:4-5) and Saul's oath (19:6) demonstrate human covenant loyalty reflecting God's faithfulness, emphasizing that God's promises and human vows play a crucial role in the unfolding of salvation history.
